summary: A 100-foot Aermotor steel lookout built in 1939 on Colville Reservation land in Washington, abandoned since 1952; non-tribal visitors need a Colville permit.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor steel tower with a cab about 7 by 7 feet
facts.agency: Colville Indian Reservation (cooperator: Colville National Forest)

access.note: The summit is on Colville tribal land. Non-tribal visitors must buy a Colville recreation permit, about $80 a year per TrailChick. TrailChick warns that access could change.

events.note: 100-foot Aermotor steel tower, the first and only lookout on the summit
Spokesman-Review item (Aug 9, 1939) reports plans for about four miles of telephone line to the new tower
Colville Examiner (July 17, 1943) reports teachers working as summer fire lookouts; one teacher is placed on Armstrong Mountain
Site abandoned; the ground-level living quarters and the lookout roof have since disappeared
Registered April 11, 2022 as US 1521, WA 70; nominated by Brad Eells

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 4,552 ft (1,387 m), firelookout.com gives 4,587 ft and TrailChick gives 4,600 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure, which matches the brief's elevation_m of 1387.4.

notes_for_editor: Height 100 ft converted to 30.5 m. Elevation conflicts across four sources; NHLR figure kept. TrailChick describes climbing the tower; the story reports that its 2017 visitor did not climb to the top and does not claim that tribal permission is needed to climb. Named 1943 teacher omitted from the story. Access rules and TrailChick's permit detail come from a 2017 visit updated in 2023; check the Colville permit page before relying on it. Living New Deal not used.
